title: Investigation of treatment expectancy in patients with atopic dermatitis undergoing a modern system therapy
summary: Many people in Germany suffer from atopic dermatitis (AD), also known as neurodermatitis. It is a persistent inflammation of the skin that leads to great limitations of the quality of life of affected individuals. In recent years, better drugs have come into the clinic to provide good treatment for moderate and severe cases of AD. However, we know that not only the pure drug effect plays a role in the clinic, but also the expectation of the patients with which they start a therapy. This expectation has an influence on the so-called "placebo effect" and can significantly affect the success of a treatment. We are interested in the factors that shape the expectations of AD patients and how these expectations affect the success of AD treatment. To this end, we want to use questionnaires and computer procedures to determine various psychological measures before and during therapy. In addition, we want to see to what extent the blood values of the patients change during this time. To get a realistic impression of patients' everydays lives, symptom burden and treatment satisfaction are regularly assessed using a smartphone application. We hope that this study will enable us to further improve the care of patients with AD.

interventions.name: Patients with atopic dermatitis who are initiated on systemic therapy will complete various questionnaires prior to initiation and after 4 and 16 weeks on therapy. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with atopic dermatitis and indication for initiation of systemic therapy.
- Women of childbearing potential with contraception (according to the Standard of Care)
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy and breast-feeding; lack of willingness to use effective contraception.
- Insufficient ability to communicate in the German language or lack of understanding of the German language; dementia or (functional) illiteracy.
- Lacking or absent capacity of the patient to give consent
- Presence of contraindications to systemic therapy with an IL-4 and IL-13 blocker or a JAK inhibitor.
